description: Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a beloved Indian classic known for its rich, creamy tomato-based sauce and tender pieces of marinated chicken. This iconic dish offers a delightful balance of sweet, tangy, and savory flavors, making it a comforting and satisfying meal. It is perfect for a special lunch or dinner, best enjoyed with naan bread or fragrant basmati rice.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, turmeric, red chili powder, garam masala, and salt. Mix well to coat all pieces. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of ghee or butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary, and cook until browned and mostly cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Set aside the cooked chicken.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add the remaining 1 tablespoon ghee or butter. Add green cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the finely chopped onion and cook until soft and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.

instructions.title: Build the Flavor
instructions.text: Stir in ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add turmeric powder, red chili powder, garam masala, cumin powder, and coriander powder. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly, to toast the spices and release their aromas.

instructions.title: Simmer the Sauce
instructions.text: Add the tomato puree to the pan. Blend the soaked cashews with a little water to form a smooth paste and add to the sauce. Stir well. Add sugar and salt to taste. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and the oil separates. Add water or broth as needed to reach desired consistency.

instructions.title: Finish the Dish
instructions.text: Remove bay leaf, cinnamon stick, and cardamom pods if desired (or blend the sauce if you prefer a very smooth texture). Stir in the cooked chicken. Add heavy cream and crushed Kasuri Methi. Simmer for another 5 minutes to allow flavors to meld and chicken to heat through, ensuring it is fully cooked.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and serve hot with warm naan bread, roti, or fragrant basmati rice for a complete and satisfying Indian meal.

tips: For the most tender chicken, marinate overnight. Grilling or pan-frying the chicken separately before adding to the sauce ensures a lovely char and locks in flavor.

Achieve a silky-smooth sauce by pureeing the cooked makhani sauce (after removing whole spices) with an immersion blender or in a regular blender, then straining it through a fine-mesh sieve before adding the chicken and cream.
Always finish your Butter Chicken with a good swirl of fresh heavy cream and a sprinkle of crushed Kasuri Methi (dried fenugreek leaves) for that quintessential authentic aroma and richness.
article:
Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani: Your Ultimate Guide to a Beloved Indian Lunch Recipe

Few dishes capture the heart and palate quite like Butter Chicken. Known traditionally as Murgh Makhani, this iconic Indian curry is a symphony of flavors – creamy, tangy, subtly sweet, and wonderfully aromatic. It’s a dish that transcends borders, gracing menus in high-end restaurants and humble eateries alike, and for good reason. Its tender chicken, luxuriating in a rich, velvety tomato and butter-based gravy, offers an unparalleled comfort that makes it a perfect choice for a satisfying lunch. If you’ve ever dreamed of recreating that restaurant-quality Butter Chicken at home, this comprehensive guide will walk you through every step, ensuring a delicious and authentic experience.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a classic Indian dish originating from Delhi in the 1950s. Legend has it that it was created by Kundan Lal Gujral, the founder of Moti Mahal restaurant, to utilize leftover tandoori chicken. He simmered the grilled chicken in a rich tomato gravy enriched with butter and cream, and thus, a culinary legend was born. The name "Murgh Makhani" literally translates to "chicken with butter" (Murgh meaning chicken, and Makhani meaning buttery), perfectly describing its core essence.

At its heart, Butter Chicken features succulent pieces of boneless chicken, often marinated in yogurt and spices, then grilled or pan-fried until lightly charred. These chicken pieces are then bathed in a luxurious gravy made from puréed tomatoes, onions, cashews (for richness), ginger, garlic, and a medley of aromatic spices like cardamom, cinnamon, and fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi). The generous addition of butter and cream at the end creates its signature silky texture and mild, balanced flavor profile, making it appealing to even those new to Indian cuisine.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting the perfect Butter Chicken requires a selection of fresh ingredients and a well-stocked spice cabinet.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color, less heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice

For the Gravy:
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more for finishing
*   1 tablespoon cooking oil
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 green cardamom pod
*   1 cinnamon stick (1-inch piece)
*   2 cloves
*   1 bay leaf
*   400g canned crushed tomatoes (or 3-4 medium fresh tomatoes, puréed)
*   1/4 cup raw cashews (soaked in warm water for 15 minutes, optional but recommended)
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder
*   1 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1/2 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 tablespoon kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), lightly crushed
*   1-2 tablespoons sugar or honey (to balance tanginess)
*   1/2 cup heavy cream, plus extra for garnish
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Follow these steps to create an authentic and delicious Butter Chicken for your next lunch.

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring the chicken is evenly coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, or even overnight for maximum flavor and tenderness.
2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer (cook in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding). Cook for 3-5 minutes per side, until lightly browned and cooked through. The chicken doesn’t need to be fully cooked at this stage, as it will simmer further in the gravy. Remove the chicken and set aside.
3.  **Prepare the Gravy Base:** In the same pan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter with the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste, cardamom pod, cinnamon stick, cloves, and bay leaf. Sauté for another minute until fragrant.
4.  **Build the Gravy:** Stir in the crushed tomatoes (and soaked cashews if using). Add the red chili powder, ground coriander, ground cumin, and a pinch of salt. Mix well and bring to a simmer. Cover the pan and cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have softened and the oil begins to separate from the mixture.
5.  **Blend the Gravy:** Remove the whole spices (cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, bay leaf). Allow the mixture to cool slightly. Carefully transfer the gravy base to a blender or use an immersion blender. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. For an extra silky texture, pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot.
6.  **Finish the Gravy:** Return the smooth gravy to the pot over medium-low heat. Stir in the garam masala, crushed kasuri methi, sugar or honey, and a generous knob of butter (another 1-2 tablespoons). Simmer gently for 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.
7.  **Combine and Serve:** Add the cooked chicken pieces to the simmering gravy. Stir gently to coat the chicken. Pour in the heavy cream and stir. Simmer for another 2-3 minutes, just until heated through and the chicken is fully cooked. Do not boil vigorously after adding cream. Taste and adjust salt and sweetness if needed. Garnish with fresh cilantro and a swirl of extra cream before serving.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving that authentic restaurant-style Butter Chicken is within reach with these expert tips:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. Longer marination (4+ hours) ensures incredibly tender and flavorful chicken that truly absorbs the spices.
*   **Don't Overcook Chicken:** When initially cooking the chicken, aim for a nice sear and light char. It will finish cooking in the gravy, so don't let it dry out in the first step.
*   **Blend Until Silky Smooth:** For that signature velvety texture, blend the gravy base thoroughly. Straining it through a fine-mesh sieve afterward is an extra step that makes a noticeable difference.
*   **Quality Tomatoes:** Use good quality canned crushed tomatoes (San Marzano if possible) for a consistent flavor and color, or ripe, sweet fresh tomatoes.
*   **Kasuri Methi is Essential:** Dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi) impart a unique, slightly bitter, and aromatic flavor that is characteristic of Butter Chicken. Toast them lightly in a dry pan for a few seconds before crushing them in your palm to release their full aroma.
*   **Balance Sweet and Tangy:** The amount of sugar or honey needed will depend on the acidity of your tomatoes. Taste and adjust to achieve a perfect balance. A touch of lemon juice at the end can also brighten the flavors.
*   **Don't Skimp on Butter and Cream:** These are defining ingredients for Murgh Makhani. They provide the richness, smoothness, and luxurious mouthfeel that makes this dish so irresistible.

## Serving Suggestions

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with a variety of accompaniments, making it an ideal Indian lunch recipe.

*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or fragrant jeera rice (cumin rice) is a classic pairing, perfect for soaking up every last drop of the rich gravy.
*   **Indian Breads:** Warm, fluffy naan bread (garlic naan, butter naan, or plain) is essential for scooping up the creamy curry. Roti or paratha are also excellent choices.
*   **Light Sides:** A simple kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, onion with lemon juice) or a cooling raita (yogurt with cucumber and spices) can provide a refreshing contrast to the richness of the curry.
*   **Beverage:** A mango lassi is the perfect sweet and cooling drink to complement the meal.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken is a masterpiece, there are many ways to adapt it to dietary needs or preferences.

*   **Vegetarian Alternatives:** For a delicious vegetarian take, substitute the chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese) to make Paneer Makhani, or use firm tofu or mixed vegetables like cauliflower and peas for a hearty Vegetable Makhani.
*   **Dairy-Free:** To make this dish dairy-free, use coconut milk or coconut cream instead of heavy cream, and use a dairy-free butter alternative or simply cooking oil. Cashews still work perfectly for thickening.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder to your preference. For more heat, add finely chopped green chilies along with the ginger-garlic paste. For less heat, use only Kashmiri chili powder for color.
*   **Nut-Free Option:** If you have a nut allergy, you can substitute cashews with melon seeds (magaz) or sunflower seeds, or simply omit them and rely on the tomatoes and cream for thickness.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** For an authentic tandoor-like smoky flavor, you can try the "dhungar" method: place a small piece of burning charcoal in a small metal bowl in the center of the finished curry, drizzle a teaspoon of ghee over it, cover immediately for a few minutes, then remove the charcoal.

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is more than just a meal; it's an experience. Its comforting warmth and exquisite flavors make it a standout among Indian lunch recipes, perfect for a cozy weekend meal or an impressive dish for guests. With this guide, you now have all the tools to create this beloved classic in your own kitchen. So, gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to delight your senses with a truly unforgettable homemade Butter Chicken. Enjoy!
